hints: Focus on the word infectious in the question stem. What does it tell you about movement or spread compared to a non-infectious disease?
Think about the broadest definition: any type of pathogen, and any route that lets it pass from one host to another host.
walkthrough:
**Spot what infectious really means**

Think like this, infectious means it can catch and spread. So we are looking for a definition about passing something on, not just getting sick on your own.

Key idea: infectious = transmissible between hosts.

**Check for too-narrow definitions**

A good definition must include all pathogens (bacteria, viruses, fungi, protoctists) and all transmission routes. If an option only mentions bacteria, only vectors, or only viruses jumping species, it is describing one example, not the whole group.

**Pick the broad, correct definition**

Option B says symptoms are caused by a pathogen transmitted from one host to another. That covers every pathogen type and every way of spreading, so it defines all infectious diseases.

options.A: Too narrow. It only mentions bacteria from the environment, but infectious diseases can also be caused by viruses and other pathogens and can spread directly host to host.
options.B: Correct. This is the general definition: an infectious disease is caused by a pathogen that can be transmitted from one host to another.
options.C: Too narrow. Vector transmission is only one route, many infectious diseases spread by droplets, direct contact, contaminated food or water without a vector.
options.D: Too narrow. A virus mutating to infect a new species describes zoonosis or emergence, which is only one special example of infection.
